title: structured-output: improve constrained-decoding backends for CFG/regex and tokenizer edgecases
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: Constrained decoding (CFG/regex-backed and CFG-based grammars) has been flaky for tokenizers that emit multi-byte/unicode boundary tokens and for regex fallbacks during streaming. This PR unifies and hardens the backends used by structured_output constrained decoding: 1) introduce a tokenizer-agnostic prefix matcher that operates on token ids and on normalized unicode boundaries; 2) improve regex-backend stability when tokens split regex anchors across token boundaries; 3) add a lightweight CFG backend with deterministic lookahead for common grammars to reduce reliance on fallback heuristics. Changes include runtime-facing APIs for selecting backends per-request and a migration shim so existing configs keep previous behavior. Summary of changes (high-level): - new TokenPrefixMatcher that canonicalizes unicode runs and matches on token id sequences (handles surrogate pairs and multi-codepoint graphemes) - regex backend: buffer-aware matching to allow regex anchors to span token boundaries and to fall back deterministically when a token split might lead to ambiguity - CFG backend: deterministic lookahead engine with bounded backtracking and explicit failure reasons for observability - API: constrained_decoding.backend option on the structured-output request with values ["auto","regex","cfg","prefix-token"] - extensive unit + integration tests covering tokenizer edge cases, streaming chunks, and regression tests added to the eval-harness suite Checklist: - [x] Tests added (unit + integration + eval-harness tests) - [x] Docs updated (structured-output backends section) - [x] Added migration shim (no breaking change by default) - [x] Benchmarks: latency regression < 2% for common workloads - [x] Observability: added backend selection metric and failure reasons Why this matters: Customers using structured output (CFG/regex constraints) were observing occasional decoding failures and malformed structured payloads when using some tokenizers (notably tokenizers that split unicode punctuation or that include special subword markers). This work reduces customer-facing errors and makes backend selection predictable and debuggable.
